keyRules: In the open category, the maximum height is 120 m, measured as the distance from the closest point of the earth's surface — not simply straight down, so near a slope the ground beside you may also count. Within 50 m of a tall artificial obstacle (over 105 m), the entity responsible for the obstacle may request permission to fly up to 15 m above the obstacle's height.

You must register as a drone operator if your drone weighs 250 g or more (or could transfer more than 80 J of kinetic energy on impact) — this applies even to toys. Below 250 g, registration is still required if the drone has a sensor able to capture personal data, unless it qualifies as a toy under the EU Toy Safety Directive. Pilot training/certificate requirements are separate and depend on the drone's class and subcategory.

Your operator registration number must be affixed to all your drones and entered into the remote identification system (Remote ID), if the drone has one. Registration in Greece is renewed after 3 years.

Visitors from non-EU/EASA countries: if your drone requires registration (see above) and you are not already registered in another EASA state, register in Greece before flying (without a Greek tax number (AFM): a special application with a passport on the HCAA website). Residents of another EASA state register in their country of residence. Training and pilot certificates from non-EU countries are not recognised in the EU.
Third-party liability insurance is required for every drone used professionally, as well as for privately used drones of 4 kg and above (national legislation).

In Greece the minimum age is 16 — no age requirement applies to flying a class C0 drone that is a toy in subcategory A1, a privately built drone under 250 g, or under the direct supervision of a certified pilot.

Areas such as the Acropolis, Delphi and Olympia fall within Yellow/Magenta zones — flights are permitted under conditions or fully prohibited depending on the specific area, and prior approval from the HCAA is required at least 5 working days in advance.

In the open category, keep the drone within your direct visual line of sight, with the naked eye (glasses/contact lenses are allowed; binoculars or a screen do not count) — or with the help of an observer, with clear and effective communication between you at all times, so that you monitor the airspace together and avoid collisions. Follow-me mode is a separate exception, permitted up to 50 m from the pilot.
Do not fly over assemblies of people. Rules for uninvolved persons depend on subcategory, class mark and operating conditions; check the official matrix.

There is no single EU-wide distance you must keep from airports. Restrictions near airports are published as geographical zones (Article 15), whose shape and size vary from airport to airport. Before flying near an airport, airfield or heliport, check your country's official drone zone map; flying within a control zone (CTR) normally requires prior permission from air traffic control.
Night flight is permitted under the EASA open-category baseline when the required green flashing light is used, unless a current geographic zone or national rule imposes a stricter condition.
Island airports: Check the DAGR map carefully—many islands have large CTRs
importantNotes: Wildfires: flying is prohibited in zones designated by NOTAM. If you see aerial firefighting assets or receive a 112 message about a fire in the area, stop the flight immediately and land. Violations: fine, criminal prosecution, confiscation of the drone.

Archaeological sites and cultural heritage monuments require prior approval from the HCAA (at least 5 working days in advance) — they are not always fully prohibited, but are subject to strict control.
Island airports create extensive restricted zones

Do not fly over ports, hospitals, energy and telecommunications facilities, or military or government installations without prior permission from the HCAA — some military and government installations are full no-fly zones on the DAGR map (many on islands). Violations may result in fines, criminal penalties and confiscation of equipment.
The GDPR applies when identifiable individuals are recorded

fields.disclaimerText: Before every flight, always check the official sources of the Hellenic Civil Aviation Authority (HCAA) and the DAGR map. This app is a tool—not a legal authority. Greece follows EASA regulations with national additions, including, among other things, submitting an application to the HCAA at least 5 working days in advance for flights in yellow/magenta DAGR zones where flying is permitted under conditions.
